candidates.finding: Do chained claim merges preserve all judgment and vote references to the final active canonical ID?
candidates.screening_result: Current onevcat/argue master@7939e67c8479aa3b9f5d070f5e7feff8b90f876d matches Index; MIT. First-party engine.ts updateClaims resolves merged claim IDs via resolveClaimId traversing mergedInto chain with cycle guard; when merging old loser into new survivor, it rewrites every merged entry whose mergedInto pointed to the loser. Final vote prompt explicitly requests votes on active claim catalog, and buildClaimResolutions ignores inactive IDs. This contradicts the predicted transitive stale-active-ID survivor failure. Source code inspected, no source-native RED or derivative patch. AGENTS.md prescribes npm run check/test/build, not run without fix.

candidates.finding: Can whitespace and NO_ANSWER variants evade shipped two-actor infinite-loop stopping in supported nested Task.run?
candidates.screening_result: Current langroid/langroid main@5d48dbbff1593de28975a7ec54cc9c4d10704e7b (MIT), changed from Index pin 1e0f5ab. task.py increments n_no_answer_alternations on explicit NO_ANSWER within two-step interval, detects repeated messages via _maybe_infinite_loop and counts stalled steps; first-party tests/main/test_task_inf_loop.py includes Alice/Bob MockLM two-actor alternating NO_ANSWER with InfiniteLoopException. Blank/whitespace variants were not reproduced in a supported run or shown to bypass all existing guards. No live model test, patch or external PR.
candidates.blocker: Supported first-party Task.run two-actor MockLM test covers explicit NO_ANSWER alternation, but no matched source-native test proves that mixed empty/whitespace response normalization permits an indefinitely continuing nonprogress alternation. Loop patterns may already be covered by stalled-step detection. Current source has drifted substantially since Index pin; an isolated first-party MockLM fixture is needed before any fix.

candidates.finding: Does debate-round history always give an actor its opposite peer's prior position rather than its own or a stale reply?
candidates.screening_result: Current jwangkun/Pi-Multi-Agent main@d2fef0f30a762ec04eff9d8dde6cd406648955bc matches Index pin; MIT. First-party src/collaboration/llm-collaboration.ts executeDebate accumulates previous successful responses in debateHistory labelled by agent name; every next-round agent receives that shared complete previous-argument transcript. It includes the other participant's prior position rather than omitting it. Some self-history is included by deliberate shared transcript, not evidence of misdirected peer feedback. No source-native error or patch found; CONTRIBUTING requires npm test/typecheck and optional provider credentials for live examples, not needed here.

candidates.finding: Do equivalent in-root nonexistent path aliases get different arbitration resource keys permitting two conflicting nested writes?
candidates.screening_result: Current wanxunyang/mocode main@28b8e9fe3319a33a00c130a3aded9eddc3182581 (MIT), differs from Index pin b6cb603. First-party resource-lock.ts canonicalFileResourceKey(normalize(jailResolve(input))) normalizes resource keys; src/sandbox/jail.ts jailResolve resolves existing symlink paths via realpathSync, while nonexistent leaf paths use nearest existing ancestor realpath plus remaining names, enforcing in-root boundaries. Equivalent supported lexical and symlink-parent aliases therefore share the path key, contradicting the predicted duplicate owner. Existing ResourceLockManager serializes conflicting requests with abort-aware release. This is a source-only native-fit null, not proven general concurrency race-freedom. CONTRIBUTING focuses Draft PRs and native npm tests; none needed without an admitted fix.
